1256	## 5. Durable custody and failure protocol
1257	
1258	Default `opensip`/`analyze` is DURABLE_AUTHORITATIVE under CD-RT-5. The host
1259	reports retention origin DEFAULTED and durable-unbounded posture before first
1260	write; the command's documented effect is admission of the project marker and
1261	private registry/store, followed by an authoritative Run. No implicit policy
1262	file is written. Explicit retention overrides have independent byte/time/count
1263	bounds with provenance; failure to satisfy an authoritative request never
1264	silently demotes it to ephemeral. `--ephemeral` is explicitly non-authoritative,
1265	uses temporary custody, mints no authoritative commit receipt and cannot satisfy
1266	baseline adoption, repair or authoritative replay prerequisites.
1267	
1268	The storage-root admission still applies the inherited sync, backup and private
1269	custody classifications separately. A detected backup-managed root requires an
1270	explicit storage-policy choice before the first source-derived write (TM V17):
1271	select another admitted root, choose explicit ephemeral mode, or acknowledge
1272	backup custody for this invocation with `--allow-backup-custody` (or the
1273	corresponding already-admitted host storage-policy record). CI never prompts;
1274	without that explicit choice it refuses REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED with detail
1275	`storage.backup-choice-required`, before creating evidence. The acknowledgement
1276	is retained as operational custody metadata; it does not alter semantic Run
1277	identity or silently write a policy file. UNKNOWN backup status is disclosed as
1278	unknown, never as not-backed-up. Purge never claims deletion of external copies.
1279	Sync/upload roots and group/ACL exposure retain their separate admission rules;
1280	a backup acknowledgement is not a network-export or shared-storage grant.
1281	
1282	Exactly one per-project writer holds the lifecycle lease/fence through source
1283	admission, evaluation and atomic commit. Read-only clients use a consistent
1284	committed ledger snapshot and never wait while holding a lock needed by the
1285	writer. Global trust admission and revocation use the security contract's lock
1286	order. SQLite WAL, transaction settings, fsync/atomic-rename carrier and crash
1287	reconciliation retain the reviewed lifecycle carrier's native obligations;
1288	the reference model here tests the semantic transition, not OS durability.
1289	
1290	Commit order:
1291	
1292	1. Validate closure and independently replay proof; compute all final IDs.
1293	2. Write immutable blobs and descriptors to private temporary files, verify
1294	   digest/length, fsync files, atomically publish under digest, fsync directories.
1295	3. In one synchronous ledger transaction insert Run manifest, object references,
1296	   retained availability generation, baseline/other authorized pins and a commit
1297	   receipt with ExecutionId, namespace, monotonic sequence, inventory digest,
1298	   signer and immutable assurance; commit and satisfy the carrier's barriers.
1299	4. Only then acknowledge commitment. Required rendering/delivery is later and
1300	   cannot rewrite the Run. Receipt signing is operational custody evidence and
1301	   excluded from semantic IDs; the receipt authenticates RunId and inventory.
1302	
1303	A failure before step 3 publishes no authoritative Run. Orphan blobs are
1304	unreferenced and eligible for GC after reconciliation. A crash after ledger
1305	commit but before acknowledgement is `durability-undetermined` to the caller,
1306	exit 4, with an ExecutionId for read-only recovery. Recovery checks the ledger
1307	and actual objects; it returns committed or failed, never repeats a repository
1308	mutation. Duplicate retry can share a Run but has a separate attempt receipt.
1309	An acknowledged Run with missing/corrupt objects becomes partially available or
1310	corrupt; the host does not pretend it was never sealed.
1311	
1312	Sealed assurance is immutable: verified means exact identity+proof checks at
1313	seal; verifiable also commits the verification closure; replayable also commits
1314	all exact admitted producer executables and source/input closure. The default
1315	authoritative profile requires replayable retention at seal. Current
1316	availability is a separate monotonic-generation record: retained, partial,
1317	expired, purged, corrupt or unavailable, with exact missing references and
1318	cause. Availability may improve through verified restoration or regeneration;
1319	sealed assurance and historical verdict never change. A query reports both.
1320	
1321	Retention roots include every live Run's required closure, active baseline,
1322	authorized repair prerequisite and backup/export operation pin. Automatic
1323	expiry respects these pins and all independent policy bounds; it refuses a
1324	new durable admission if the required closure cannot be retained within bounds.
1325	A direct purge of a pinned Run refuses unless the explicit destructive purge
1326	also revokes the named pins after disclosing consequences. That refusal has a
1327	registered public projection and this contract does not restate it: the
1328	foundation-owned detail `evidence.pinned` projects as `request-rejected`,
1329	`REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`, exit 2, carrying the closed
1330	`common.schema.json#/$defs/PinnedPurgeDisclosure` — the RunId, the complete
1331	current `activePins` inventory sorted uniquely by `pinId`, and the three ordered
1332	consequences `named-pins-revoked`,
1333	`dependent-evidence-replay-unavailable`, `sealed-history-retained` — exactly as
1334	**workflows-and-surfaces §12** specifies. No pin is omitted, truncated or
1335	aggregated into a count. Neither that disclosure nor any flag confers authority:
1336	a later destructive attempt still requires the explicit lifecycle authorization
1337	and disclosure of its then-current complete pin set, and a changed pin inventory
1338	requires renewed disclosure before destruction. Purge retains the
1339	minimal sealed manifest, provenance and tombstone but deletes unshared evidence
1340	bytes by reachability GC; shared bytes survive until the final reference is
1341	removed. Purged is not deleted-history. The user may separately destroy the
1342	whole project store/marker under lifecycle authorization; no indefinite privacy
1343	claim is made for backups or exports already outside that store.
1344	
1345	A retention decision never changes a fact, Coverage, finding or Run identity.
1346	It never turns expired evidence into `no match`. Query of retained manifest is
1347	allowed after purge and states evidence unavailable. Query requiring actual
1348	proof, comparison baseline or repair input refuses with
1349	REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED and `evidence.{expired,purged,missing,corrupt}`
1350	before evaluation (exit 2); inability during a selected operation is HOST.IO_FAILURE
1351	with evidence detail (exit 4). Successfully admitted partial native inputs may
1352	instead produce an indeterminate Run (exit 3) under the native and D9 contracts.
1353	These are different event positions, not interchangeable error spellings.
1354	
1355	Backup/export holds a read snapshot plus short-lived object pins, writes a
1356	bounded relative-path inventory, hashes and verifies every object, then seals
1357	the bundle. Import checks path traversal, symlinks, sizes, duplicate paths,
1358	cryptographic identities and all referenced schemas before publishing anything.
1359	Source provenance/authenticity is reported separately from hash integrity.
1360	Trust floors, current authorization and local custody receipts are never
1361	restored backwards from an evidence backup. Portable baseline details are in
1362	the workflow contract. An import cannot silently claim a remote Run was locally
1363	evaluated: its imported-custody receipt names origin and local verification.

1365	## 6. Required implementation conformance
1366	
1367	Reference checks cover exact numeric and canonical encodings, wrong-source and
1368	wrong-Plan joins, identity changes for each semantic input, operational identity
1369	exclusion, universal negatives under incomplete resolution, proof tampering,
1370	retention/purge invariance and crash acknowledgement states. They additionally
1371	assert the digest law mechanically: that every 64-hex field carries a registered
1372	representation, that each new closed record reproduces an independently computed
1373	canonical digest vector and moves under every single-field mutation, and that a
1374	complete Run with a non-empty native context set closes while an altered frame, a
1375	missing preimage, a wrong preimage, an unregistered H domain, a raw payload
1376	offered as an H identity and a hidden input each refuse with a typed cause. They
1377	also assert that a fully re-framed and re-keyed Run built around a context the
1378	native boundary refuses — contradicting honored options, a compiler or runtime
1379	digest outside the tool closure, an incomplete stdlib inventory, a component
1380	digest that is not the retained tree's, a compiler version not from the manifest,
1381	a universe contradicting its context, or a config graph or lockfile path outside
1382	the snapshot — is refused with that boundary's own typed refusal string. They
1383	exercise a complete Rust universe/fact/Coverage Run alongside the TypeScript one,
1384	with the nested dependency, features, config-projection and prepared-output
1385	records retained and joined; and they separate cache key construction from cache
1386	hit admission, showing that a key needs no bytes while a hit needs the Run's whole
1387	closure. Their source pins
1388	and independent review are part of D-372. They do not qualify a native carrier.
1389	
1390	Before shipping, the exact implementation must additionally demonstrate:
1391	all supported platform fsync/SQLite/process-death cases; concurrent readers and
1392	writers plus trust revocation; independent replay across machines; missing,
1393	corrupt, stale and wrong-tenant closure rejection; hostile archive import; GC
1394	with shared references; backup restoration preserving trust floors; and public
1395	D9/CLI/JSON/SARIF/HTML/agent parity. Those are implementation acceptance criteria
1396	under existing G gates, not unresolved design alternatives.

1398	### Reference lifecycle joins
1399	
1400	The reference store instantiates closed commit-receipt and availability records.
1401	An availability transition increments generation and never rewrites a sealed Run
1402	or its original assurance. Read-only `recover(ExecutionId)` inspects the committed
1403	receipt after a lost acknowledgement and never repeats effects. Verified restoration
1404	requires the same complete identity closure and replay result before availability
1405	returns to retained; a regeneration mismatch refuses. Physical fsync, authenticated
1406	receipt signing, shared-blob deletion and OS crash recovery remain implementation
1407	qualification obligations; the reference transitions do not claim to execute them.
1408	
1409	The security chapter's three lease modes refine the inherited single-writer rule:
1410	immutable readers coexist with the append writer; exclusive migration/purge acquires
1411	the writer lease and reader exclusion. No second writer is permitted.
1412	
1413	At Run closure, every Plan-selected import re-admits its retained canonical SourceCorrespondence. An exact-snapshot import must name the Plan snapshot. VCS-revision imports require a retained, canonical admitted SourceMappingV1 to that snapshot, with inventory-matching source digests and the current clean revision; an unmapped/stale intake artifact may remain available for inspection but cannot be selected as an analyzed Plan input. Intake storage does not establish this source join. The authenticated importer/evaluator still owns payload-schema, observation-scope and polarity admission; rehashing an opaque import is insufficient. The reference closure reuses the same workflow import/mapping schema admission functions so the source law has one implementation.
1414	
1415	The semantic grant's `prepare-code` operation is present exactly when it projects trusted-repository-code preparation principals. Their provenance comes from consumed admitted host-prepared inputs; no test-runner operation or principal is added. Verification/replay checks these immutable bindings without reusing expired operational grants.
1416	
1417	The expected VCS build context is explicit, never inferred from the imported claim. The host may select one analysis-spec parameter whose schemaDigest is the raw SHA-256 of `foundation/import-source-context.schema.json` and whose payloadDigest binds canonical ImportSourceContextV1 `{schemaVersion:1, declaredBuildIds:[...]}`. These expected labels come from the separately admitted analysis request/build configuration; the importer cannot nominate its own expected labels. No parameter means an empty set; more than one is refused. Labels are declarations, not proof: source mapping remains mandatory. Run closure reconstructs workflow §4's binding from this retained parameter and the snapshot's VCS observation, then applies the same staleness function (both dirty flags, revision, expected build label and admitted mapping). A label not in the expected set is wrong-build and cannot become a Plan-selected import. The schema bytes and payload are retained with the Plan parameters for independent replay.
1418	
1419	Snapshot capture consumes the same admitted boundary inventory as native discovery. The host obtains it from successful security discovery, passes it unchanged to native discovery/membership and the shared scope descriptor, and removes nested-repository, nested-project and directory-custody-excluded paths before opening or hashing snapshot source bytes. The remaining paths are only capture candidates: per-file custody, safe handles and exact hashing still precede source admission. Boundary exclusion anchors enter the Plan's scope descriptor and their operational provenance is retained beside it. The host reference join admits one inventory; caller-supplied alternative boundary lists or substituted marker sets are refused. Discovery's dependency-tree pruning is an analysis-unit rule; explicitly required native dependency read-set bytes require separate custody/closure admission and cannot cross a nested authority boundary.
1420	
1421	Every Plan with selected import2 inputs also requires read-import in its semantic grant. This includes imported-inert preparation. Close_run enforces this operation/input join as well as prepare-code/principal equality; the later consuming-Plan admission separately validates the actual preparedResolution provenance.
1422	
1423	
1424	The reference closure entry point reports a missing promised object/blob as EvidenceUnavailable carrying the closed operational-failed/HOST.IO_FAILURE/host-io termination with evidence.missing and the missing reference. It never emits a bare lookup error or turns missing witness bytes into a false predicate or admission rejection. This models the host's retained-byte/custody observation boundary. Untrusted malformed records still receive exact schema/identity admission refusal; an inventory of available retained bytes does not authorize rewriting the assurance of a sealed Run.

90	
91	### 1.1 Cell coordinates
92	
93	A cell is `capability × languageMode × platformFamily`. The machine-readable
94	matrix is `native/native-capability-matrix.v2.json`, validated by
95	`NativeCapabilityMatrixV2`; its `cells` array is the **complete product** of its
96	own `capabilities` and `languageModes`, and the reference checks hold it to
97	exactly that product rather than to a number written here. (A literal count in
98	this prose said `60` while the matrix held 66; a second hand-maintained counter
99	would only go stale again, so the count is derived from the two arrays and
100	reported by the checks instead of restated.) Platform families are exactly the
101	four `platformId`
102	values in the delivery release inventory: `linux-x86_64-gnu`,
103	`linux-aarch64-gnu`, `macos-aarch64`, `macos-x86_64`. The OS/kernel/libc/filesystem
104	*baseline* that qualifies a machine into a family is owned by the security unit
105	(AR-06); this contract states only that native capabilities are platform-invariant
106	by design (`platformInvariantDesign: true`) and that no cell is `QUALIFIED` here.
107	
108	Cell states (closed): `SUPPORTED-DESIGN` (contracted behavior, corpus named,
109	qualification pending), `UNSUPPORTED-TYPED` (refuses with the named deficiency;
110	never silently narrows), `NOT-SELECTED` (outside D-371; no promise).
111	
112	### 1.2 Language modes (closed)
113	
114	| Mode id | Recognition | Universe | Notes |
115	|---|---|---|---|
116	| `ts-tsconfig` | `tsconfig.json` at the unit root (or named by discovery), `allowJs` absent/false | `typescript-v2`, `configOrigin=tsconfig` | JavaScript files are not program roots; a JS import target is `unresolved-module-specifier`. |
117	| `js-allowjs` | `tsconfig.json`/`jsconfig.json` with effective `allowJs=true` (jsconfig defaults `allowJs=true`) | `typescript-v2`, `allowJs=true` | `.js/.mjs/.cjs/.jsx` are program roots. |
118	| `js-synthesized` | No `tsconfig.json`/`jsconfig.json` at the unit root; `package.json` present or any `.js/.mjs/.cjs/.jsx` file under the unit | `typescript-v2`, `configOrigin=synthesized`, `synthesizerVersion=1` | Host synthesizes `SynthesizedCompilerOptionsV1` (§2.2); Plan-bound with `DEFAULTED` provenance, disclosed in output. |
119	| `rust-cargo` | `Cargo.toml` at the unit root (package or workspace) | `rust-v2` | Requires a sealed `DependencySourceSetV1` when the lock lists any non-path package (§3). |
120	| `rust-cargo-prepared` | as above, plus an admitted `PreparedOutputSetV3` of inert rows | `rust-v2` with `preparedOutputSetId` non-null | Expansions and directives are consumed as data; a site without a row is an unresolved edge (§3.6). |
121	| `syntax-only` | any file whose extension maps to a bundled grammar | `syntax-v2` (grammar-only; no compiler) | Inventory/syntax/clones only; semantic rungs `language-tier-unsupported`. |
122	
123	**The syntax-only universe (CB3-MUST-3).** This column previously read
124	"none (syntax-all provider)", and that made the mode's own advertised cells
125	unrepresentable. `fact2` and `subject-scope` both **require** a
126	`native-semantic-universe` h-identity, that domain set held exactly the
127	TypeScript and Rust universes, and there is no null branch — so a
128	`declares@syntactic` or `clones@normalized-body-hash` fact in `syntax-only`
129	mode, and every `file`/`package`/`vcs-change` fact in a repository containing
130	no TypeScript and no Rust unit at all, could mint no fact and no scope. An
131	implementer had to invent a third domain, invent a null branch on a required
132	identity field, or quietly narrow this table.
133	
134	The registered answer is a third universe, `native.semantic-universe.syntax.v2`,
135	over a third native context, `native.context.syntax.v2`. Making the universe
136	fields nullable was rejected: it would delete the invariant that every fact
137	states what produced it, and would leave "which grammar read this body"
138	unanswerable for exactly the facts that depend on the answer.
139	
140	- **What it carries.** The context holds one thing: the installed
141	  `SyntaxGrammarBundleV1`, pinned the way a toolchain is — an admitted
142	  `kind=grammar` closure, a `parserVersion` that must equal that closure
143	  manifest's `semanticVersion`
144	  (`native.syntax-grammar-version-not-from-manifest`), and every grammar
145	  definition, the bundle manifest and the normalizer specification present in
146	  the retained tree. It has no toolchain, no stdlib, no lockfile, no
147	  `node_modules` layout and no config graph, because a grammar-only analysis
148	  reads none of them. A syntax-only context that named a compiler would assert
149	  semantics the mode never computes.
150	- **What the universe commits.** The admitted context plus the **selected**
151	  grammar set. Selecting a different set is a different universe, exactly as
152	  selecting different compilation targets is for Rust, so what was parsed is
153	  visible to every consumer instead of being an invisible default. A selection
154	  naming a grammar the bundle does not contain refuses
155	  (`native.syntax-grammar-not-in-bundle`). The constant
156	  `resolutionAttempted=false` is carried so no consumer can read the universe
157	  as a resolution claim.
158	- **The body dialect axis.** `body-language-version.dialect` gains a third
159	  branch, `{grammarVariant}`. A syntax-only analysis has no compilation unit, so
160	  it has no edition to select and no program to join; claiming `{edition: 2021}`
161	  for a `.rs` body read without Cargo would fabricate compiler semantics. One
162	  suffix must map to one grammar
163	  (`native.syntax-grammar-suffix-ambiguous`), longest match wins, and a suffix
164	  with no bundled grammar refuses rather than being folded into a neighbour —
165	  which is what keeps `unsupported-file / no-bundled-grammar` an honest
166	  classification. Because it is a distinct branch, **a grammar-parsed body never
167	  mints the same identity as a compiler-parsed one over the same bytes.** That
168	  is required: a grammar parse and a compiler parse are different
169	  interpretations, and equating them would be a false clone claim.
170	- **Capability is not widened.** A `syntax-only` universe carries only the
171	  inventory rungs, the `syntactic` rungs and `clones@normalized-body-hash`.
172	  `imports`/`references`/`calls`/`types`/`reachability` remain
173	  `language-tier-unsupported` under it, `unresolved-edge` stays unavailable
174	  because no resolution was attempted, and a universal-negative predicate still
175	  requires its own complete `CoverageResultV3`. Nothing here lets a syntax-only
176	  Run claim a resolved or type fact.
177	- **The bundled grammar set is closed, and it has SEVEN languages.** The host
178	  bundles grammars for `rust`, `typescript`, `javascript`, `json`, `toml`,
179	  `markdown` and `yaml`; the shared discovery rule routes all fourteen of their
180	  suffixes to membership `syntax-only`, reason `grammar-only`. An earlier
181	  revision of this section let the grammar descriptor name only the three code
182	  languages and asserted equality with the `body-language-version` `languageId`
183	  enum as a drift check. That check proved the enum matched itself: it could not
184	  express the four data/document grammars the host has always shipped, so the
185	  promise directly above — *any* file whose extension maps to a bundled grammar —
186	  was unrepresentable for them. The descriptor now covers exactly the bundled
187	  set, and each row declares its **`syntaxClass`**.
188	
189	**`code` versus `data-document`: the distinction the contracts already draw.**
190	This is not a new narrowing; it is an existing law made machine-readable.
191	
192	- **`code`** — `rust`, `typescript`, `javascript`. §6.3 defines body spans as
193	  function, method, closure/lambda, `impl` item and block bodies, publishes the
194	  L2/L3 normalisation tables for exactly these languages, and puts
195	  `languageId ∈ {typescript, javascript, rust}` in the clone preimage. These
196	  grammars bear clone body identity and the code-construct syntax relations, and
197	  their `languageId` **must** be a member of the `body-language-version` enum.
198	- **`data-document`** — `json`, `toml`, `markdown`, `yaml`. These formats have no
199	  such body spans, and this kit publishes **no** tokenisation, `literalKind`
200	  mapping or normalisation law for them anywhere. Their files are grammar-only
201	  members — accounted, inventoried, and never `unsupported-file` — bearing
202	  `file`/`package`/`vcs-change` inventory evidence under the syntax universe.
203	  They mint **no** body identity, no suffix of theirs appears in the grammar
204	  dialect table, and their `languageId` **must not** be in the
205	  `body-language-version` enum, since it could never appear in a clone preimage.
206	
207	Both directions are enforced at grammar-bundle admission: a data grammar
208	claiming `code`, a code grammar demoted to `data-document`, and a row claiming a
209	suffix the discovery table routes to another language each refuse with their own
210	typed cause. What is held equal to the `body-language-version` enum is therefore
211	the **`code` subset**, not the whole bundle — which accounts for all seven
212	languages instead of ignoring four.
213	
214	Claiming `declares`/`literal`/`control-flow` facts for a data format would
215	require a tokenisation law this kit does not publish, and inventing one would be
216	precisely the fabricated-semantics failure the syntax-only universe exists to
217	prevent. If the product later wants data-format syntax facts, it needs a
218	published tokenisation and `literalKind` law first; that is a bounded future
219	capability and this matrix does not promise it today.
220	
221	An unbundled language stays unrepresentable: `.py` has no bundled grammar, is
222	not in the descriptor vocabulary, and its files remain `unsupported-file` with
223	reason `no-bundled-grammar`.
224	
225	**The capability law binds facts and Coverage, not just descriptors.** Validating
226	a grammar bundle's declared `syntaxClass` constrains what a bundle may say about
227	itself; it does not constrain what a Run may claim. An earlier revision enforced
228	the registry only there, and full Runs consequently admitted a Markdown-anchored
229	`declares` fact, a **complete** empty `declares`/`clones` Coverage over a
230	data-only repository, and `references@resolved-binding` under a universe whose
231	own record declares `resolutionAttempted: false`. The registry is therefore
232	consulted at the two boundaries that decide what a Run asserts, and at neither
233	does it consult the claimed coverage value, the caller-declared class, or
234	whether facts happen to exist:
235	
236	- **Every admitted fact.** A `fact2` under a syntax universe is admissible only
237	  if **every one of its anchor paths** is read by a **selected** grammar whose
238	  registry capability set contains that `relation@rung`. The anchor is the file
239	  the body was actually read from, so a Markdown-anchored code fact refuses in a
240	  mixed repository exactly as it does in a data-only one
241	  (`SYNTAX_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED_FACT`). **Inventory capabilities are exempt
242	  here as well as at the scope boundary below** — the exemption belongs to the
243	  *relation*, not to the boundary. An earlier revision wrote this bullet as an
244	  unconditional every-anchor rule and stated the exemption only in the scope
245	  bullet, so the two bullets contradicted each other: a literal implementer
246	  refused a `file@enumerated` fact for `tool/main.py` while the scope bullet had
247	  just promised that the same path's inventory Coverage was unconditionally
248	  `complete` — an inventoried file that is authoritatively absent. An inventory
249	  fact is not read by a grammar at all; it *is* the inventory row, the manifest
250	  declaration or the VCS observation, so there is no grammar for it to be gated
251	  on. (The relation registry's `anchorLaw` independently gives the inventory
252	  class **zero** anchors, so such a fact names no anchor path for this bullet to
253	  test either; the two laws agree and neither leans on the other.) The exemption
254	  is from grammar ownership **only**: the relation's snapshot joins, own-scope
255	  attribution and the anchor law all still bind, and no code fact becomes
256	  admissible because some other anchor in the Run sits on a supported path.
257	- **Every requested scope, including an empty view.** A `subject-scope` under a
258	  syntax universe is judged on its committed **examined extent** — the source
259	  inventory of the snapshot it names. **Inventory** capabilities
260	  (`file@enumerated`, `package@manifest-declared`, `vcs-change@vcs-reported`) are
261	  **always** available and are deliberately **not** grammar-gated: a snapshot
262	  inventories every file it contains, including ones no bundled grammar reads,
263	  and requiring a grammar per inventory row would silently narrow that promise.
264	  A **code** capability requires at least one path in that extent to be read by a
265	  selected `code` grammar. A capability no selected grammar bears is unavailable —
266	  which is every semantic rung and `unresolved-edge` under a syntax universe,
267	  exactly as the matrix already says.
268	
269	**A promised inventory capability represents every inventoried path, and a
270	`complete` inventory result may not hide an omitted one.** These are two halves
271	of one promise and the second was missing. `file@enumerated` is **total** over
272	the snapshot inventory: a snapshot inventories exactly the files it contains, so
273	every inventoried path has exactly one `file` fact, and over a **complete**
274	`file@enumerated` Coverage the predicate `exists file where path=P` is
275	authoritative. A complete result that retains no fact for an inventoried subject
276	therefore asserts that an inventoried file is absent, and that graph closed —
277	nothing derived the obligation, so nothing compared it. A `complete`
278	`file@enumerated` Coverage must now carry an admitted `file@enumerated` fact for
279	every one of its subjects that the snapshot inventory contains
280	(`COVERAGE_INVENTORY_TOTALITY_OMITS_PATH`), derived at Run closure from the
281	retained view's own facts and the retained inventory.
282	
283	**A fact discharges the obligation of the scope it actually belongs to.** The
284	match is on every coordinate the registry's `matchOn` lists — the four
285	`CoverageKeyV2` coordinates other than the commitment itself
286	(`relation`, `resolution`, `sourceUniverse`, `targetUniverse`) plus the owning
287	`snapshotId`. Matching relation and rung *alone* is not enough in a view carrying
288	more than one universe, and this is not hypothetical: the view-level fact/scope
289	join is **existential** — each fact need only agree with *some* scope on relation,
290	rung and both universes — so a TypeScript `file` fact is lawfully present in a
291	view that also carries a syntax-universe `file@enumerated` scope, and while the
292	match was two-coordinate it *paid that scope's missing-file obligation*. A
293	complete Run exhibited exactly that: two `complete` scopes over `a.ts`, only the
294	TypeScript fact, admitted. Totality is a claim about what **this** universe
295	examined, so it must be discharged by evidence produced in this universe; a fact
296	from another universe is a different interpretation of the same bytes, not the
297	same observation. The two-universe Run in which *each* scope carries its own fact
298	remains lawful and is retained as a positive control. `snapshotId` is listed
299	although Run closure already forces it on every fact and scope: this law reads one
300	scope's obligation out of a *shared* view, and a join that silently leans on an
301	invariant enforced elsewhere is the same implicit coupling that produced the
302	cross-universe defect.
303	
304	Two things the law deliberately does not require: a subject the snapshot does
305	**not** contain is owed nothing —
306	the host examined the question and the file is genuinely absent, which is the
307	one case a universal negative over inventory exists to serve — and an `unknown`
308	result carrying its disclosed deficiency is owed nothing, which keeps a
309	partially examined inventory representable rather than forcing a false
310	`complete`. `package@manifest-declared` and `vcs-change@vcs-reported` are **not**
311	total and owe nothing: most paths declare no package and most were not changed,
312	so their empty results are ordinary findings. Which relations owe totality is
313	stated in the relation registry (`coverageTotality`), where only `file` has a
314	row, and never inferred.
315	
316	**How many spans a fact cites is a registry law, not an implementer's choice.**
317	`fact.anchors` carried no `minItems`, and only `clones` ever stated a
318	cardinality, so every published predicate over the array — the `file` row's
319	`anchorPathField`, and the every-anchor rule above — was universally quantified
320	and therefore *vacuously true* at zero anchors. It neither permitted nor forbade
321	the unanchored spelling, and both spellings of one `file@enumerated` claim closed
322	a Run with different `fact2` identities. The relation registry now carries a
323	closed `anchorLaw` on every relation, in three classes: `source-text` (the nine
324	code relations) needs **at least one** span, because a code fact is read from
325	source text and an unanchored one names no file that could have been read;
326	`body-identity` (`clones`) is **exactly one**, unchanged; and `inventory`
327	(`file`, `package`, `vcs-change`) is **exactly zero**, because such a fact's
328	whole semantic input is its payload, which the relation's own snapshot joins
329	already bind. Zero is also the only cardinality *every* inventoried path can
330	satisfy — including a `vcs-change` whose `changeKind` is `deleted`, whose path is
331	by construction not in the snapshot and can carry no anchor at all. The
332	`source-text` class deliberately imposes **no additional relation-specific
333	maximum** and no canonical extent *beyond the common schema bounds* —
334	`fact.anchors` already carries `maxItems: 100000` and `uniqueItems`, and those
335	continue to apply to every relation; what the class declines is a per-relation
336	ceiling or a canonical span set, not the shared one. Which spans a producer cites
337	is a real statement about what it read, so two producers citing different spans
338	have produced different semantic descriptors and legitimately mint different
339	identities. Nothing here promises cross-provider anchor identity for code facts. Two things this also closes that the previous
340	wording did not: an unanchored *code* fact was refused only inside this
341	syntax-universe guard and closed a Run under a TypeScript or Rust universe, and
342	`anchorPathField` existed only on the `file` row, so a `package` fact anchored
343	into an unrelated file closed a Run. One law now covers every relation in every
344	universe (`FACT_ANCHOR_CARDINALITY`).

347	universe identity, so a bundle that ships a Rust grammar the universe did not

350	**An unavailable request is disclosed, not answered, and never refused outright.**
351	The capability is retained and representable: the scope closes a Run and carries
352	`coverage: unknown` with `deficiency: language-tier-unsupported` and
353	`nativeCause: capability-missing` — both already in the existing vocabulary, and
354	mapped in §10. A **false `complete`** for an unavailable capability, a wrong or
355	null cause, and a wrong deficiency each refuse with their own reason

357	`…_DEFICIENCY_MISMATCH`). No syntax Run is made blanket-indeterminate to achieve

361	The guard is **syntax-universe specific**. Every capability of the TypeScript and
362	Rust universes is unchanged, including all five semantic relations, and the Rust
363	compilation-ownership guards are untouched — see the ownership disclosure law in
364	§10, whose prerequisite is now derived from the actual universe kind so that a
365	grammar-only clone scope, which has no compilation unit at all, owes no
366	compiler-ownership obligation.
367	
368	**A scope is judged on ITS OWN extent where the published law supplies one.** The
369	relation registry states, per relation, what `subject-scope.subjects` identify
370	(`subjectKindLaw`). For a **`source-path`** relation — `clones`, `file`,
371	`vcs-change`, which bind their subject to a snapshot path through their registry
372	`snapshotJoins` `pathField` or, for `clones`, through the single `bodyIdentityJoin`
373	anchor — the subjects **are** the extent, and **every** named path must be
374	supported. So a `README.md`-scoped clone request is unavailable even in a mixed
375	snapshot that also contains `src/plain.rs`: an unrelated code file elsewhere does
376	not serve it, and a scope naming both cannot hide its unsupported part behind its
377	supported one.
378	
379	For a **`symbol`** relation the subjects are opaque `SubjectIdV1` values that the
380	retained record associates with **no** path. The enumerator's attribution of
381	symbols to files is **trusted** and is not re-derivable from the retained Run, so
382	the only answerable question is the coarser one — can this universe produce this
383	capability anywhere in the committed extent — and that is what is asked. Treating
384	a symbol identifier as a path would reject lawful code scopes, and inventing
385	symbol-to-path parsing would be fabricated evidence. This is a stated
386	trust-boundary limit, not an oversight, and a mixed-repository empty `declares`
387	scope therefore remains admissible.
388	
389	**Path support is decided by the SELECTED grammar ROWS and their own suffixes**,
390	not by the set of selected languages. The descriptor permits a row to own a
391	**subset** of its language's bundled suffixes, and two rows of one language may
392	own disjoint suffixes; admission requires only that a claimed suffix belong to
393	that language and that no suffix be claimed twice. A selected TypeScript row
394	owning `.ts` therefore establishes nothing about a `.tsx` path when no selected
395	row owns `.tsx`, and longest match runs over the union of the selected rows' own
396	suffixes so `.d.ts` still resolves through a row owning `.ts`. An unanchored code
397	fact is **not** vacuously supported: it names no file that could have been read.
398	
399	**`allowJs` and `checkJs` are not completeness claims** (feedback 11; primary
400	sources `typescriptlang.org/tsconfig/allowJs` and `/checkJs`, read 2026-09-06).
401	`allowJs` is a *program-membership* option: it admits JavaScript roots. `checkJs`
402	is a *diagnostics* option: it reports errors in JavaScript files and changes
403	nothing about what is resolved. Both are universe keys (they change PlanId);
404	neither gates a capability, and neither implies that resolution was attempted or
405	complete. Resolution completeness is asserted only by `CoverageResultV3` (§4.3).
406	The universe carries `jsAdmittedToProgram`, `jsDiagnosticsEnabled` and the
407	constant `resolutionCompletenessImplied=false` so no consumer can confuse them.
408	
409	Module systems inside `typescript-v2` are observed, not chosen: `import`/`export`
410	and `require()`/`module.exports` are both resolved by the pinned compiler under
411	`module=node16` semantics keyed by `package.json` `type`. A non-literal specifier
412	is an unresolved edge (§4.4), never a silent drop.

675	  `capabilityId` refuses rather than merging, because two rows declaring
676	  different applicable modes for one capability would leave default selection
677	  ambiguous.
678	
679	**The registry states availability; it never states scope.** An earlier revision
680	said "the registry may declare a **subset** of the matrix — a release need not
681	ship everything". That sentence was written about *membership* and reads as
682	permission about *scope*, and it is corrected here, because the default was
683	driven **from** the registry: a staged build shipping three rows silently
684	requested three capabilities and still looked conformant. That is the D-371
685	selected product quietly shrinking with nothing disclosed anywhere, against this
686	section's own promise that the default is the full registered set and against
687	admission §1.1's complete intended product.
688	
689	- **Required default (fixed by the matrix, not by a release).** For each
690	  discovered unit the `default` profile **must** request every capability whose
691	  `(capability, unit languageMode)` cell is not `NOT-SELECTED` — the published
692	  definition of the selected product, since `NOT-SELECTED` means "outside D-371;
693	  no promise". `UNSUPPORTED-TYPED` cells are **included deliberately**: the matrix
694	  says such a cell "refuses with the named deficiency; never silently narrows",
695	  and the way it never silently narrows is that the default asks and the Run
696	  answers with the disclosed unavailable pair. Omitting it would leave a consumer
697	  with no record that the capability exists and was not served.
698	- **Absence is disclosed, not dropped — and delivered.** A capability the product
699	  requires and this release does not declare available is still requested, and the
700	  selection boundary records the absence in `default_capability_selection`'s
701	  `undeclaredCapabilities`. That record is an **availability account, not a
702	  `CoverageResultV3`** and not a final `(deficiency, nativeCause)` pair — and, on
703	  its own, it is a helper return, not something a consumer receives. An earlier
704	  revision stopped there and called it "machine-readable"; an in-memory result is
705	  not a delivered disclosure.
706	- **The public carrier, named — and it delivers in *this* invocation.** One
707	  analysis step's selection produces the `{noticeCount, notices[]}` leaf
708	  (`release_absence_notices`); adding its `stepId` forms a
709	  `CapabilityAvailabilityStepV1`, and the invocation's steps compose
710	  `CapabilityAvailabilityV1` = `{stepCount, totalNoticeCount, steps[]}`
711	  (`invocation_availability`), carried on **`CommandEnvelope.availability`**.
712	  Each notice carries the **complete ownership tuple in typed fields** —
713	  `capabilityId`, `languageMode` and the unit's own `workspaceRoot` — with the
714	  code `native.capability-unavailable` and the registered remedy. Two things this
715	  fixes: an earlier revision concatenated `<capabilityId> @ <languageMode>` into
716	  a `subject` and **discarded `workspaceRoot`**, so two units requesting the same
717	  capability collapsed into one indistinguishable notice; and it had no carrier
718	  for *multiple* absences in the original invocation at all, since
719	  `StepTermination.domainDetail` is singular and a `doctor` report is a
720	  **different invocation**. The tuple is never concatenated: `workspaceRoot` is a
721	  `UserInputPath` bounded at 4096 while `BoundedText` is 1024, so concatenation
722	  could silently truncate a path.
723	- **Composed per step, because 1024 is the analysis-spec bound.** Each analysis
724	  step's own selection becomes a `CapabilityAvailabilityStepV1`
725	  (`{stepId, noticeCount, notices[≤1024]}`), and the invocation carries
726	  `{stepCount, totalNoticeCount, steps[≤64]}`. A *step's* collection cannot
727	  truncate — 1024 is exactly the `analysis-spec.requestedCapabilities` bound and
728	  one selection yields at most one absence per requested row — but the invocation
729	  is **not** bounded by that number: a named multi-step invocation carries up to
730	  64 steps, and two admitted selections of 1023 requests each compose 2046
731	  notices, which one flat 1024 array refused. Composing per step preserves every
732	  valid admitted invocation and **discards no notice to fit**; `steps` is bounded
733	  by the invocation's own step bound (`StepId` 0–63).
734	- **Association, order and count.** Each entry names the `stepId` whose selection
735	  produced it. A step that made **no** selection contributes no entry; a step
736	  that selected and found nothing absent contributes an entry with an **empty**
737	  array, which is the positive statement that it checked; a retried step
738	  contributes one entry, for the attempt whose selection the invocation retained.
739	  The same ownership tuple may recur in **different** steps, so uniqueness is
740	  within a step and never across the invocation. `noticeCount` equals each step's
741	  array length and `totalNoticeCount` is their sum — stated invariants, not a
742	  truncation policy. Order is the selection's own, under
743	  `x-opensip-order: sequence`. `AnalysisResult` is a closed union and is **not**
744	  widened.
745	- **The notice's code is its condition.** `code` is `const
746	  native.capability-unavailable`, not the whole `DomainDetailCode` enum: this
747	  typed record declares exactly one condition, and an earlier revision admitted
748	  `CONFIG.INVALID` on a release-absence notice.
749	- **Declared parity, not merely envelope membership.** Being present on the
750	  envelope does not make a field part of renderer parity — `render` selects only
751	  a command's declared `parityFields`, so the collection reached JSON and agent
752	  and was omitted by human, SARIF and HTML. `capability-availability` is now a
753	  declared parity field of every `requestClass: analysis` command (`default`,
754	  `analyze`, `fit`, `audit`, `repair-verify`), so every applicable renderer
755	  carries it.
756	- **Authority limits.** The disclosure is **advisory**: it terminates nothing,
757	  mints no Coverage, creates no Control verdict and no repair authority, and
758	  fabricates no clone `Candidate` — the published Candidate records represent
759	  actual candidates, so an absent provider can never be one. Nothing here
760	  truncates: a step's `notices` is bounded by the analysis-spec request bound it
761	  can never exceed, and `steps` by the invocation's own step bound, so
762	  `noticeCount` and `totalNoticeCount` are exact rather than a residue of a
763	  dropped tail.
764	- **Which capabilities use which route.** A **fact-producing** capability keeps
765	  its `relation@rung` Coverage under the existing precedence, and this detail
766	  does not replace it. A **candidate-only** capability has no Coverage entry at
767	  all, so this detail is its *only* public route. No new vocabulary, no new
768	  public code, **no preview or default exception**.
769	- **What an absence projects to, and what wins when two apply.** Neither case may
770	  be assumed. *Precedence*: a capability can be undeclared **and** unservable by
771	  the admitted universe at once — `references` under `syntax-only` is both. The
772	  syntax capability prerequisite *derives* `language-tier-unsupported` /
773	  `capability-missing` for such a scope and refuses anything else, and §10's
774	  precedence ranks `language-tier-unsupported` ahead of `provider-unavailable`,
775	  so the more specific one wins and the release-absence account never overrides
776	  it. Where no more specific deficiency applies, `provider-unavailable` with
777	  `capability-missing` is the applicable pair on the existing
778	  `COVERAGE.PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` route. *Candidate-only capabilities*:
779	  `clones-near` and `clones-cross-tsjs` have **empty** matrix `relations` — they
780	  are candidate-only by §6.1 authority, mint no fact and no `relation@rung`, and
781	  therefore have **no Coverage entry** that could carry a pair; requiring one
782	  would mean fabricating a relation. Their account is the selection record itself
783	  (`projection: selection-account-only`), while fact-producing capabilities carry
784	  `projection: coverage-entry` and name the exact `relation@rung` coordinates
785	  they project onto. An availability account may be shared by all capabilities;
786	  it is automatically a Coverage result for none of them.
787	- **Availability is not qualification.** Declaring a capability cannot promote a
788	  cell: `platformQualified` stays false, no cell is `QUALIFIED`, and
789	  `SUPPORTED-DESIGN` remains "contracted behavior, corpus named, qualification
790	  pending" whatever a release declares. A staged or development build shipping
791	  fewer providers is an availability fact disclosed per request — not a narrowed
792	  product and not a completed release qualification.
793	- **Explicit configuration overrides the request, not the obligation.**
794	  `product-configuration.analysis.capabilities` uses this same vocabulary; an
795	  override is a recorded choice with its own provenance (the default's is
796	  `DEFAULTED`). A user narrowing their own analysis is visible; a host silently
797	  narrowing the product would not be.
798	- **The host input boundary, honestly.** *Which* rows a release ships is an
799	  authenticated input this contract cannot measure, and nothing here qualifies a
800	  build, an installer or a provider. What is contract is the obligation the
801	  default must meet, the membership the declaration is held to, and the
802	  disclosure an absence owes.
803	- **Closed at admission, not only in the helper.** The default helper is one
804	  producer of an `analysis-spec`, not the authority. The same vocabulary is
805	  closed again at Plan/Run closure over the **retained** `analysis-spec`
806	  (`ANALYSIS_SPEC_CAPABILITY:native.requested-capability-*`), so an explicitly
807	  configured or hand-built spec is judged by exactly the rule a defaulted one is,
808	  and the default and explicit paths agree on one spelling by construction. The
809	  foundation keeps its own fault for an unregistered *mode*; native owns which
810	  capabilities exist and which cells this product promises anything for.
811	
812	No capability is added, removed or renamed, no cell state changes, and all six
813	advertised modes, the three native contexts and the full default-selected
814	product stay exactly as representable as before. What is new is the authority
815	for a field that had none.
816	
817	**Backup custody join.** Dependency-source files, inert prepared rows and
818	generated-file blobs are host CAS objects under the one host storage root; they
819	inherit the identity-and-evidence §5 backup-managed-storage choice
820	(`--allow-backup-custody` or an admitted storage-policy record; CI without a
821	choice refuses `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED` / `storage.backup-choice-required`).
822	Native adds no second store and no custody rule of its own.
823	
824	`mixed-native-partial` fixes the meaning: TypeScript unit complete, co-located Rust
825	unit missing an external crate → TypeScript-scoped predicates evaluate;
826	repository-scoped semantic predicates are indeterminate with
827	`input-closure-incomplete` naming the crate; syntax and clone predicates complete
828	for both.

832	## 2. Semantic universe successors
833	
834	Every array in the current native schema bundle declares `x-opensip-order`
835	under identity §3. `sequence` preserves order and repeated items unless a separate
836	uniqueness constraint applies. It is intentional for compiler flags, signature
837	tokens, substitution precedence and ordered observations. Stricter orders are
838	machine-checked at schema admission: declaration components by `component`,
839	dependency packages by `(name, version, sourceId)`, owner records by `ownerKey`,

840	file-manifest rows by `path`, and the explicitly sorted path/name/enum collections
841	by raw UTF-8 bytes. These keys must be unique; a second row with the same key and
842	different payload also refuses. The canonical encoder never sorts a collection.
843	Input-adapter observation sequences retain their own declared order; a producer
844	must construct any stricter output collection before admitting it.

870	**Binding a `rust-v2` universe (`bind_rust_universe`).** A universe is bound to its
871	admitted context before PlanId, exactly as `typescript-v2` is bound by
872	`bind_typescript_universe` (§2.4), and for the same reason: an identity commits to
873	the context bytes, not to the universe's copy of them. The binding is pure — it
874	executes no cargo, rustc, build script, proc macro or filesystem read — and takes
875	the admitted context descriptor, the retained nested input records
876	(`DependencySourceSetV1`, `UnifiedFeaturesV1`, `PreparedOutputSetV3` when one is
877	selected) and the analysed snapshot inventory. All three are **required**: there is
878	no context-free or input-free admit path, because an optional join is not a rule,
879	and omission is the typed refusal `native.universe-retained-inputs-not-supplied`,
880	never an ADMIT. It refuses when
881	
882	- the admission is not a Rust context admission, or the universe names a context
883	  this host did not mint, or the supplied context bytes are not the admitted ones;
884	- any overlapping field disagrees:
885	  `dependencySourceSetId`, `unifiedFeaturesId`, `preparedOutputSetId`, `rustflags`,

892	  dependency set, toolchain, cfg set or preparation kind;
893	- a prepared output set is retained but **no** universe selected it
894	  (`preparedOutputSetId = null`): optional absent preparation stays absent, and
895	  bytes in custody never enter a resolution by being in custody;
896	- the snapshot does not contain what the universe names: `Cargo.lock` missing or

901	consumed, never an execution grant; retained inert prepared bytes cannot imply one,

A tree in which two paths share a basename refuses `native.native-context-stdlib-tree-ambiguous-basename:<name>` rather than resolving the join arbitrarily |
1044	| `toolchain.libSelection` | the effective `lib` **names** the resolved `compilerOptions` select after `target` defaulting, sorted; each must map to a retained component under the published name-to-component join below. These are `lib` names (`es2022`), never declaration-file names |
1045	| `toolClosure.compiler`, `toolClosure.runtime` | raw digests of the bundled compiler and of the bundled JavaScript runtime that executes it, both members of the signed closure named by `closureId`. No `PATH` lookup, no system `node`, no `NODE_OPTIONS`/`NODE_PATH`/`TS_NODE_*` from the environment |
1046	| `configProjection.honoredOptions` | the closed subset of the **effective** resolved `compilerOptions` (or of `SynthesizedCompilerOptionsV1` under `js-synthesized`) that changes program membership, module resolution or checking |
1047	| `configProjection.strippedOptions` | every option removed, with a typed reason (`selects-an-executable`, `emits-output`, `reads-the-environment`, `acquires-types-from-the-network`, `not-a-resolution-or-membership-option`). Stripping is disclosed here and is never a reason to read the option from anywhere else. `typeAcquisitionEnabled` and `executableSelected` are schema constants `false` |
1048	| `configProjection.configGraphPaths` | every `tsconfig`/`jsconfig` file of the resolved `extends` graph, in the snapshot, sorted by logical path; empty under `configOrigin=synthesized` |
1049	| `nodeModulesLayoutDigest` | raw SHA-256 of `C(ResolvedNodeModulesLayoutV1)` — the retained resolution read-set layout — or `null` exactly when `nodeModulesInReadSet=false` |
1050	| `lockfileIdentity` | `{kind, path, contentSha256}` of the admitted lockfile, or `null` when `lockfileKind=none` |
1051	
1052	**Retained trees.** The stdlib closure and the compiler closure are retained **whole** —
1053	complete foundation `closure` descriptor and complete file tree — and joined to the selected
1054	compiler. `admit_native_context` recomputes each closure identity from its retained record
1055	and refuses `native.native-context-closure-unretained`,
1056	`native.native-context-closure-identity-mismatch` or
1057	`native.native-context-closure-kind-mismatch` before any digest comparison. The stdlib merkle
1058	root is therefore never a bare number a caller can assert.
1059	
1060	**`libSelection` → `standardLibraryComponentDigests`: the published join.** The
1061	two arrays hold different vocabularies on purpose and neither is rewritten into
1062	the other. `libSelection` holds effective **`lib` names** — the values
1063	`configProjection.honoredOptions.lib` carries (`es2022`, `dom`), which is why the
1064	two are compared directly. `standardLibraryComponentDigests[].component` holds
1065	**declaration-file basenames** of the retained stdlib closure tree
1066	(`lib.es2022.d.ts`). Because the join between them is enforced at context
1067	admission with its own typed refusal, it is published here rather than left to
1068	ecosystem convention; two hosts inventing different mappings would admit and
1069	refuse the *same* retained context bytes differently, which is a public admission
1070	divergence, not implementation freedom.
1071	
1072	| Rule | Statement |
1073	|---|---|
1074	| Fold | `fold(n)` is Unicode **Default Case Conversion `toLowercase(X)`**: the **full**, **non-tailored**, **context-sensitive** default lowercase mapping (Unicode Standard §3.13 / UAX #21). It is the **same single fold** the honored-`lib` agreement below uses, and this section defines no other: no NFC/NFKC step, no trimming, no alias table, no prefix or suffix matching. Reference implementation `native_evidence_model.v2.lib_name_fold` |
1075	| Mapping | `component(n) = "lib." + fold(n) + ".d.ts"`. Total, deterministic and **one-directional**: a selected name maps to exactly one component basename, and a component is never mapped back into a selected name |
1076	| Membership | for every `n` in `libSelection`, `component(n)` must be an element of the declared `component` set. A name whose component is absent refuses `native.native-context-lib-not-retained:<n>` — §10 route `request-rejected` (2) / `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`, before PlanId |
1077	| Equality | `{fold(n) : n ∈ libSelection}` must equal `{fold(m) : m ∈ honoredOptions.lib}`. `honoredOptions.lib` is required and non-empty in the closed resolved context, so this agreement always applies and is **not** weakened by the mapping. Two `libSelection` entries with the same fold refuse `native.native-context-field-mismatch:duplicate-lib-selection`; a set disagreement refuses `native.native-context-field-mismatch:libSelection` |
1078	| Order | `libSelection` is sorted by the raw UTF-8 bytes of the **retained, unfolded** names; `standardLibraryComponentDigests` by the raw UTF-8 bytes of `component`. Each record keeps its own specified order for hashing — folding is a comparison, never a rewrite of a retained value, and neither array is re-spelled into the other's vocabulary |
1079	
1080	**What `fold` is, and what it is not.** The three plausible operations are genuinely different
1081	and only one of them is the one this admission performs, so it is named rather than approximated.
1082	
1083	| Discriminator | `fold` (**full default lowercase**) | simple lowercase | case folding |
1084	|---|---|---|---|
1085	| `U+0130` LATIN CAPITAL LETTER I WITH DOT ABOVE | `U+0069 U+0307` — **two** code points, through `SpecialCasing.txt` | `U+0069`, one code point | `U+0069 U+0307` |
1086	| `U+039F U+03A3` (sigma in **final** position) | `U+03BF U+03C2` — the `Final_Sigma` condition | `U+03BF U+03C3` | `U+03BF U+03C3` |
1087	| `U+03A3 U+039F` (sigma **not** final) | `U+03C3 U+03BF` | `U+03C3 U+03BF` | `U+03C3 U+03BF` |
1088	| `U+00DF` LATIN SMALL LETTER SHARP S | `U+00DF` — unchanged | `U+00DF` | `U+0073 U+0073` |
1089	
1090	So `fold` is **not** `Simple_Lowercase_Mapping` (it expands, and it is position-dependent) and
1091	**not** `Case_Folding` (sharp s is unchanged). It is **non-tailored** — the root locale, with no
1092	Turkish/Azeri dotless-i and no Lithuanian tailoring — so the result must never depend on an ambient
1093	locale, an environment variable or a host language setting.
1094	
1095	**Version custody, and the portability consequence it does not hide.** The result of a default case
1096	conversion is determined by the Unicode case data the host carries, so `fold` is deterministic
1097	**given a case-data version**, and this design binds the reference derivation to one:
1098	`native_evidence_model.v2.UNICODE_CASE_DATA_VERSION`, currently **UCD 15.0.0**, the version the
1099	table above was measured against. Two hosts on different case data can fold the same name
1100	differently — for a code point unassigned in one of them (an unassigned code point folds to itself),
1101	or for one whose mapping changed between the versions — and because `libSelection` enters the
1102	context descriptor and therefore `PlanId`, that would be an admission divergence, not a cosmetic
1103	one. This contract does **not** claim the fold is invariant across every runtime. It requires the
1104	version to be a declared, checkable property rather than whatever the runtime happens to ship:
1105	`unicode_case_data_agreement()` reports the running version against the declared one so drift is
1106	disclosed instead of silently changing an outcome. Nothing here narrows the field to ASCII to
1107	sidestep the question — it is simply true that every `lib` name in the pinned compiler's own option
1108	vocabulary is ASCII, where all three operations above coincide, and that is a fact about the current
1109	vocabulary rather than a constraint on the value.
1110	
1111	**Custody: the two arrays answer different questions.** `libSelection` is the
1112	*configuration-facing* record of what the resolved options selected, and it is
1113	what the universe/config agreement is checked against.
1114	`standardLibraryComponentDigests` is the *tree-facing* **complete** declaration
1115	inventory of the retained stdlib closure — one row per `.d.ts` member with its
1116	raw digest, selected or not. So the selection never narrows the inventory and the
1117	inventory never adds a selected name: a missing inventory row refuses
1118	`native.native-context-stdlib-inventory-incomplete:<basename>`, and a tree in
1119	which two paths share a basename refuses
1120	`native.native-context-stdlib-tree-ambiguous-basename:<basename>` — the mapping's
1121	target would not be unique, and an arbitrary resolution is exactly what this
1122	refusal exists to prevent. The join reads **no other input**: not a
1123	caller-supplied map, not a filesystem lookup, not a compiler query, not the
1124	`typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot` value on its own.
1125	
1126	**No platform *field*, and the identity is still platform-specific.** Unlike the Rust context there
1127	is no `targetTriple`/`hostTriple`, because TypeScript *resolution semantics* — which specifiers
1128	resolve, which subjects are examined, what is checked — are platform-invariant by design (§1.1).
1129	That is a design selection of this contract, not a measurement, and it is **not** a claim that the
1130	identity is platform-invariant: `toolClosure.closureId` names a signed closure whose foundation
1131	`closure` descriptor includes `platform`, so the same source analysed with the platform-specific
1132	executables of two families mints two `nativeContextId`s — as it must, because different bytes ran
1133	(`typescript-context-identity-is-platform-specific-through-its-signed-tool-closure`).
1134	
1135	**Universe and Plan binding.** `typescript-v2.nativeContextId` is
1136	`H("native.context.typescript.v2", descriptor)` in the `Sha256Text` form. `PlanId` binds the
1137	same digest through `plan.nativeContextDigests`, which takes the **bare 64 hex** (§11, the
1138	foundation `plan` record's spelling) and is a canonical **set**: several units of one language
1139	legitimately share one context, and identical admitted contexts collapse to one member — that is
1140	deduplication of an identical descriptor, never of two different ones.
1141	
1142	`bind_typescript_universe(universe, admission, context)` refuses a universe whose `nativeContextId`
1143	this host did not mint (`native.universe-context-binding-mismatch`) and refuses a Rust-minted context
1144	outright (`native.native-context-language-mismatch`). The **retained context bytes are a required
1145	argument**: there is no context-free admit path, because an optional field-agreement check is not a
1146	rule — a caller that omitted it would obtain exactly the bypass this join exists to close. Omission
1147	is the typed refusal `native.universe-context-not-supplied`
1148	(`typescript-universe-bound-without-the-retained-context-refuses`); context bytes that do not hash to
1149	the admitted id refuse
1150	`native.universe-context-binding-mismatch:context-bytes-are-not-the-admitted-ones`.
1151	
1152	Given those bytes the two records must **agree where they overlap**: a matching `nativeContextId`
1153	commits to the context bytes, not to the universe's copy of them, so `languageMode`,
1154	`packageModuleType`, `allowJs`, `checkJs`, `lockfileKind`, `nodeModulesInReadSet`,
1155	`jsDiagnosticsEnabled`, `jsAdmittedToProgram`, `configOrigin`, the `extends`-graph emptiness and the
1156	synthesized-options presence are each checked against the context and refuse
1157	`native.universe-context-field-mismatch:<field>`.
1158	
1159	The context itself also has mandatory agreement rules. `moduleResolutionMode`
1160	equals `configProjection.honoredOptions.moduleResolution`. `libSelection` is
1161	strictly sorted by UTF-8 name bytes, contains no duplicate names under the
1162	published `fold`, and selects the same folded name set as the honored `lib` list
1163	— the same `fold` the component join above uses, and the only one this section
1164	defines; each record retains its specified order for hashing. The closed resolved context
1165	always materializes that nonempty list. When source configuration omits `lib`,
1166	the resolver supplies the pinned compiler's target-default library selection
1167	in both records; `null` is not an alternate resolved spelling.
1168	`standardLibraryComponentDigests`
1169	has strictly unique component keys in UTF-8 order. Context admission refuses any
1170	contradiction before its digest may enter Plan. In synthesized mode every value
1171	in `synthesizedOptions` equals the corresponding honored option, and an absent
1172	optional `jsx` means honored `jsx` is null. Presence alone is insufficient.
1173	These are semantic agreement checks in addition to closed schema validation;
1174	internal diagnostic suffixes remain operational refusal evidence, not new public
1175	DomainDetail codes.
1176	
1177	**Independent derivation (§9.5) applies to TypeScript exactly as to Rust.** The worker
1178	recomputes the context from its own sealed inputs; a differing byte is
1179	`Unavailable(native-context-mismatch)` before Analyze.

1206	
1207	### 3.1 `DependencySourceSetV1`
1208	
1209	Identity domain `native.dependency-source-set.v1`. Closed descriptor:
1210	`{schemaVersion:1, language:"rust", lockfileIdentity, packages:
1211	[DependencyPackageSourceV1…] sorted by (name, version, sourceId) UTF-8 bytes,
1212	completeness:{state, missing[]}}`.
1213	
1214	`DependencyPackageSourceV1`:
1215	
1216	| Field | Rule |
1217	|---|---|
1218	| `name`, `version` | exact `[[package]]` values from `Cargo.lock` |
1219	| `sourceKind` | `registry \| git \| path \| vendored` |
1220	| `sourceId` | exact `source` string from `Cargo.lock`, or `""` for path packages |
1221	| `lockChecksum` | 64-hex from the lock `checksum`, or `null` for git/path |
1222	| `fileManifestSha256` | H(`native.dependency-file-manifest.v1`, sorted `[{path, contentSha256, byteLength}]`) |
1223	| `fileCount`, `totalBytes` | exact uint64 |
1224	| `acquisition` | `{mode: in-snapshot-path \| in-snapshot-vendored \| imported-descriptor, descriptorId: ImportId\|null, vendorPath\|null}` |
1225	| `checksumVerification` | `tarball-matched \| self-consistent \| not-applicable \| mismatch` — `mismatch` refuses the whole set |
1226	| `provenanceAssurance` | `registry-authenticated \| declared` |
1227	
1228	Verification rules (feedback 3 corrected):
1229	
1230	- **DS-1 (registry, vendored tree)** A vendored directory carries a self-asserted
1231	  `.cargo-checksum.json`. Its `package` field equalling `lockChecksum` proves
1232	  nothing about the files: an attacker rewrites file contents and every `files`
1233	  entry while preserving `package`. The host therefore checks internal
1234	  consistency only (`package == lockChecksum`, every listed file's SHA-256
1235	  matches, no extra or missing files) and records `checksumVerification =
1236	  self-consistent`, `provenanceAssurance = declared`. Inconsistency is `mismatch`
1237	  and refuses the set. The reference model contains the mutation
1238	  (`ds1-mutation-preserving-package-checksum-stays-declared`): the mutated tree is
1239	  still admitted, and it is still *declared*, never authenticated.

1240	- **DS-2 (registry, tarball)** Only the exact `.crate` tarball whose SHA-256
1241	  equals `lockChecksum` yields `tarball-matched` / `registry-authenticated`. The
1242	  host extracts it deterministically into the CAS and computes the file manifest
1243	  itself. An extracted tree plus `.cargo-checksum.json` is DS-1.
1244	- **DS-3 (git)** The import supplies the checked-out tree for the exact `#rev`;
1245	  `not-applicable` / `declared`; the file manifest identity is the binding.
1246	- **DS-4 (path)** Path dependencies live in the snapshot; nothing is imported.
1247	- **DS-5 (no ambient reads)** `$CARGO_HOME/registry`, `~/.cargo`, `vendor/`
1248	  outside the snapshot, or any host path is read **only** as the explicit,
1249	  user-named source path of an import step (§7). Any acquisition mode outside the
1250	  closed set, or any fetch URL, refuses. No network fetch exists in any first-party
1251	  code path (design invariant, conformance-checked; not a confinement claim).
1252	- **DS-6 (completeness)** The set is complete for a target when every package
1253	  activated by `UnifiedFeaturesV1` is present with `checksumVerification ≠
1254	  mismatch`. An incomplete set is admitted with `completeness.incomplete` and
1255	  typed `input-closure-incomplete` Coverage for dependent crates; it never blocks
1256	  syntax analysis.
1257	
1258	`declared` provenance is disclosed wherever the package matters: in the Plan
1259	(through the set descriptor), in `AuthorizedExecutionV2.owners[].provenanceAssurance`,
1260	and in the pre-execution sentence (§5.2). Facts derived from declared sources are
1261	still Plan-bound Coverage inputs; the disclosure is what changes.
1262	
1263	### 3.2 Custody and transport
1264	
1265	The host stores admitted dependency sources in its content-addressed store keyed
1266	by `fileManifestSha256`; Plan-bound by `dependencySourceSetId`. Transport uses
1267	protocol-3 frames `DependencySourceManifest / DependencySourceChunk /
1268	DependencySourceSeal / DependencySourceAccepted` (§9.2) with the same byte-exact,
1269	digest-verified, reject-before-use discipline as the snapshot. The worker mounts
1270	the accepted files read-only at `.opensip/deps/v1/<name>-<version>/…` in its
1271	private scratch materialization. Nothing is fetched lazily.

1273	### 3.3 Cargo configuration: verified carrier, exact flags (feedback 5, 10)
1274	
1275	Primary source (`doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html`, read 2026-09-06):
1276	Cargo reads `.cargo/config.toml` (and legacy `.cargo/config`) from the current
1277	directory and **every ancestor**, plus `$CARGO_HOME/config.toml`, merging arrays;
1278	it also honors `CARGO_*` environment overrides and knobs that select executables
1279	(`build.rustc`, `build.rustc-wrapper`, `target.*.linker`, `target.*.runner`),
1280	credentials and network. Stock Cargo has no switch that disables ancestor
1281	discovery, and this contract does not claim `--config` replaces the stack.
1282	
1283	The first-party `opensip-cargo-adapter` therefore establishes a **verified
1284	ancestor carrier** (`CargoConfigProjectionV2`, all checked by
1285	`cargo_config_admission` in the model):
1286	
1287	- **CC-1** Before every Cargo invocation, every ancestor directory of the private
1288	  scratch root is checked for `.cargo/config.toml` and `.cargo/config`. Presence
1289	  is a refusal (`native.ambient-cargo-config`, exit 4), never a merge and never a
1290	  silent skip. `ancestorCarrierVerified=true` is recorded in the context.
1291	- **CC-2** `CARGO_HOME` is a fresh private empty directory created for the
1292	  invocation; its `config.toml` is absent by construction.

1295	  presence of any is a refusal. Tool locations are passed as absolute closure
1296	  paths on the command line, not via environment.

1298	- **CC-5** Every `.cargo/config(.toml)` inside the snapshot (any directory, not
1299	  only the root) is replaced in the materialization by the single projected file;
1300	  the originals remain snapshot bytes for identity but are never read by Cargo.

1304	`source.<name>.directory` pointing inside the snapshot with `replace-with`,

1374	- **PO-0 (inert by kind and consumption channel; a media type is a label, never a
1375	  trust proof)** Admissible row kinds are exactly three:
1376	  `build-script-directives` (`text/x-cargo-directives`: the captured `cargo:`
1377	  lines, including `rustc-cfg`/`rustc-env` consumed by `cfg`/`env!`),

1379	  invocation `site` = `{path, startByte, endByte, inputTokenDigest}`), and
1380	  `generated-file` (`generated = {logicalPath, blob}` with media type
1381	  `text/x-rust-source`, `text/plain` or `application/octet-stream`: one data file
1382	  a build script wrote under `OUT_DIR`). Row kinds `proc-macro-dylib` and
1383	  `build-script-binary` are refused **regardless of the media type they claim**
1384	  (a dylib relabelled `text/x-rust-expansion` is still a dylib row), and a media
1385	  type outside the kind's set is refused; either is
1386	  `native.prepared-output-not-inert` (exit 2), from an import *and* from the
1387	  in-host step alike (`generated-file-media-type-is-not-trust-proof-kind-decides`).

1389	  worker.** Expansions are looked up by exact
1390	  `(path, span, inputTokenDigest, macro crate manifest)`; a miss is a
1391	  `macro-expansion-unavailable` edge (L-RS4).

1393	  The worker resolves `env!("OUT_DIR")` for owner *O* to the read-only virtual
1394	  path `.opensip/out/v1/<ownerKey>/` in its sealed VFS. A site
1395	  `include!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), "/generated.rs"))` (likewise
1396	  `include_str!`/`include_bytes!`) reads the `generated-file` row bound to
1397	  `(ownerKey, logicalPath="generated.rs")` whose `inputBinding` equals the current
1398	  context, and consumes its bytes **only** as Rust source text, a string literal or
1399	  a byte literal respectively. A miss (no row, stale binding, failed owner) is a
1400	  typed unknown: `build-script-generated-unavailable` edge, cause
1401	  `generated-file-missing`; it is never a hard failure and never a fallback to a
1402	  host path (`generated-file-include-out-dir-resolves-inert`,
1403	  `generated-file-missing-is-typed-unknown-not-failure`). Strict bounds
1404	  (`GeneratedInputBoundsV1`): `logicalPath` is a strict relative path (no `/`
1405	  prefix, no `.`/`..` segment, no NUL or backslash, ≤ 1024 bytes; an escaping path
1406	  fails exact typed admission and the worker lookup independently refuses it with
1407	  cause `generated-file-out-of-bounds`), `maxGeneratedFilesPerOwner 4096`,
1408	  `maxGeneratedFileBytes 67108864`, `maxGeneratedTotalBytes 1073741824`,
1409	  `maxGeneratedFileRows 1000000` (protocol limit). Imported blobs are bound to
1410	  archive members by exact `blobs[]` digest; an archive member outside the
1411	  wrapper's `blobs` is never read (`generated-file-path-escape-and-bounds-refused`).
1412	- **PO-1 (staleness)** A row is usable only if `inputBinding` equals the current
1413	  context (owner manifest, dependency set, toolchain digest, cfg set). A stale row
1414	  is refused before Plan construction (`REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`, detail
1415	  `native.stale-prepared-output`, listing the differing fields) when prepared mode
1416	  was selected explicitly, or is ignored with a disclosed `staleRows` list and
1417	  non-prepared fallback when prepared mode was defaulted. It never uses a stale blob.
1418	- **PO-2 (failed rows)** A `failed` build script is retained as a row so the same
1419	  inputs need not be re-run; the owner is analyzed non-prepared
1420	  (`build-script-generated-unavailable`).
1421	- **PO-3 (imported)** An imported set carries the same binding fields and
1422	  `provenanceAssurance: declared`; the host cannot verify that an external
1423	  preparer produced the expansions faithfully. Facts derived from them are
1424	  Plan-bound and disclosed with the import identity and producer.
1425	
1426	Where do the expansions and generated files come from? From the **preparation
1427	step** (§5.3), which is the only place proc-macro dylibs are built and loaded and
1428	build scripts run, inside the authorized `repository-code` principal with live
1429	boundaries. The step captures the required generated **data** and discards every
1430	executable product; its output is the inert row set, and the worker consumes only
1431	that.
